newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco to sell majority shares in oil refineres.
newsitem.headline: Morocco to sell majority shares in oil refineres.

text.p: Morocco will soon cede up to 51 percent in oil refineries Samir and SCP to a core of investors, including foreigners, a ministry official said on Wednesday.
"The announcement of the sell-off of up to 51 percent, respectively, in the Samir and SCP oil refineries is imminent," an official at the privatisation ministry told Reuters.
The official, who declined to be identified, said the state holds 67 percent of Samir and 73.8 percent of Societe Cherifienne des Petroles (SCP).
He declined to give the date of the official announcement.
The Minister of Privatisation Abderrahman Saaidi, who will directly supervise the privatisation of both firms, was not immediately available for comment.

The government floated 30 percent of Samir on the Casablanca bourse at $310 million in March 1996. It had promised to sell up to 51 percent by the end December 1996, but nothing was achieved, mainly because of tough negotiations with foreign investors.
A Casablanca Finance Intermediation stockbroker said the privatisation of both companies "would be good news for the market...It also will end the recent speculation in Samir shares."

The Societe Marocaine de l'Industrie du Raffinage (Samir) has a capacity of six million tonnes a year and refines 80 percent of the country's domestic oil products. SCP processes the remaining 20 percent.
